Figure S3.2

Likelihood judgments by condition

Note. Density plots of the primary sample’s responses by outcome condition, with one panel for each legal context. Lines mark the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th percentiles. No information is the foresight condition. Expected evidence is the HACE condition, and unexpected evidence is the HUCE condition. Each density is drawn only within the range of its scale (0 to 100 for each of the three likelihood ratings). The figure is descriptive and includes no test. Primary sample n per condition: illegal abortion, 68 with no information, 63 with expected evidence, and 63 with unexpected evidence; improper disposal, 71 with no information, 66 with expected evidence, and 67 with unexpected evidence.

Figure S3.3

Consequence severity, foreseeability, and evidence relevance by condition

Note. Density plots of the primary sample’s responses by outcome condition, with one panel for each legal context. Lines mark the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th percentiles. No information is the foresight condition. Expected evidence is the HACE condition, and unexpected evidence is the HUCE condition. Each density is drawn only within the range of its scale (1 to 7 for consequence severity, 1 to 5 for foreseeability, and 1 to 9 for evidence relevance). Evidence relevance is the mean of the 10 relevance ratings. The figure is descriptive and includes no test. Primary sample n per condition: illegal abortion, 68 with no information, 63 with expected evidence, and 63 with unexpected evidence; improper disposal, 71 with no information, 66 with expected evidence, and 67 with unexpected evidence.

Figure S3.4

Judgments of the detective by condition

Note. Density plots of the primary sample’s responses by outcome condition, with one panel for each legal context. Lines mark the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th percentiles. No information is the foresight condition. Expected evidence is the HACE condition, and unexpected evidence is the HUCE condition. Each density is drawn only within the range of its scale (1 to 7 for decision quality and 0 to 10 for detective blame, the consequences for the detective, and the wrongness of the decision). The figure is descriptive and includes no test. Primary sample n per condition: illegal abortion, 68 with no information, 63 with expected evidence, and 63 with unexpected evidence; improper disposal, 71 with no information, 66 with expected evidence, and 67 with unexpected evidence.

Figure S3.5

Suspect blame by condition

Note. Density plots of the primary sample’s responses by outcome condition, with one panel for each legal context. Lines mark the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th percentiles. No information is the foresight condition. Expected evidence is the HACE condition, and unexpected evidence is the HUCE condition. Each density is drawn only within the range of its scale (1 to 7). The figure is descriptive and includes no test. Primary sample n per condition: illegal abortion, 68 with no information, 63 with expected evidence, and 63 with unexpected evidence; improper disposal, 71 with no information, 66 with expected evidence, and 67 with unexpected evidence.

Figure S3.6

Confidence in the probable cause ruling by condition

Note. Density plots of the primary sample’s responses by outcome condition, with one panel for each legal context. Lines mark the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th percentiles. No information is the foresight condition. Expected evidence is the HACE condition, and unexpected evidence is the HUCE condition. Each density is drawn only within the range of its scale (0 to 100 for probable cause confidence and −100 to 100 for signed probable cause confidence). Signed confidence is the confidence rating when the participant found probable cause and its negative when the participant did not. The figure is descriptive and includes no test. Primary sample n per condition: illegal abortion, 68 with no information, 63 with expected evidence, and 63 with unexpected evidence; improper disposal, 71 with no information, 66 with expected evidence, and 67 with unexpected evidence.

Figure S3.7
